## Discovery & Translational Science

- **[Big Pharma]** **Renal arteriolar GLP1R expression is significantly depleted in human diabetic kidney disease** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.18.26368399)
  - Single-cell spatial transcriptomics of 2,531 renal arterioles from kidney biopsies across diabetic kidney disease (DKD, n=28), other non-diabetic glomerular diseases (n=102), and healthy living donors (n=24) demonstrated a ~20% loss of contractile smooth muscle cells in DKD arteriolar walls.
  - Smooth muscle cell expression of *GLP1R*—the receptor target of GLP-1 receptor agonists—was detected in only 0.48% of remaining arteriolar smooth muscle cells in DKD, compared to 1.21% in non-diabetic glomerular diseases and 1.75% in living donors.
  - Smooth muscle regulatory genes *GRIA2* and *PRDM6* were also selectively downregulated in DKD arterioles, highlighting specific target cell depletion in microvascular remodeling.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Gly716Arg β-myosin mutation impairs contractile kinetics and mavacamten sensitivity in HCM** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.19.767856)
  - Subcellular functional analysis of human ventricular myofibrils isolated from hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) patients bearing the Gly716Arg (G716R) β-myosin mutation revealed prolonged relaxation kinetics compared with healthy donor myofibrils.
  - The force-inhibitory response to mavacamten was significantly blunted in G716R myofibrils, and the drug failed to reverse mutation-induced relaxation slowing under conditions simulating elevated diastolic calcium levels.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Circulating immune features predict response to neoadjuvant pembrolizumab in early TNBC** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.19.26368490)
  - Flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing (135,271 cells) of peripheral blood from 64 patients with early triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) treated with pembrolizumab-based neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy revealed baseline transcriptional differences between responders and non-responders.
  - Non-pathological complete response (non-pCR) patients exhibited systemic baseline enrichment of TNF-α/NF-κB, MYC, and mTORC1 signaling pathways in cytotoxic T cells and NK cells.
  - Patients achieving pCR maintained preserved naive and memory T-cell profiles, alongside enriched CX3CR1-expressing CD4 memory populations prior to treatment.

- **Circulating gelsolin and longitudinal proteomic panels track ALS functional decline** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.18.26368465)
  - Serum proteomic profiling (5,401 proteins) across four independent cohorts (Sheffield, Oxford, Tel Aviv, and Answer ALS) identified 68 non-NfL plasma proteins that correlated with individual ALS disease stage (fraction of onset-to-death interval elapsed).
  - Serum gelsolin and markers including CLEC3B, ANTXR2, and ART3 mapped within-patient functional decline rate, establishing systemic inflammation and muscle remodeling panels distinct from motor neuron-derived neurodegeneration markers [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.15.26368153).

- **Fermentable fiber lowers intestinal pH to control blood pressure via GPR65** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43064734/)
  - Preclinical research demonstrated that gut microbial fermentation of dietary fiber reduces large intestinal pH, which directly activates the proton-sensing G-protein coupled receptor GPR65 to induce systemic blood pressure lowering.

- **SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages identified as driver target in papillary thyroid cancer** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43064763/)
  - Multi-omics analysis identified SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages as central mediators of tumor microenvironment remodeling, lymph node metastasis, and adverse therapeutic response in papillary thyroid carcinoma.

- **Baseline plasma proteomic signature predicts anti-TNF remission in Crohn's disease** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.18.26368439)
  - Prospective proteomic profiling (SomaScan, 7,322 analytes) in pediatric and young adult Crohn's disease patients undergoing infliximab or adalimumab therapy derived a candidate 73-protein signature predictive of combined endoscopic and clinical deep remission.

- **Longitudinal plasma biomarkers track long-term clinical progression in early Parkinson's disease** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.18.26368420)
  - Evaluation of baseline plasma neurodegeneration markers in 523 early sporadic Parkinson's disease patients from the PPMI cohort confirmed that elevated baseline P-tau217, neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) independently track multi-year clinical motor and cognitive decline over up to 11 years of follow-up.

- **Semaphorin 3G evaluated as biofluid biomarker for cerebral amyloid angiopathy** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.18.26368450)
  - Proteomic evaluation across CSF (n=1,982) and plasma (n=6,917) datasets demonstrated marked reductions of Semaphorin 3G (SEMA3G) in Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia, with biofluid levels inverse to lobar cerebral microbleed burden on MRI.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **Preoperative roxadustat evaluated in Phase 2a elective surgery trial** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43064581/)
  - A Phase 2a randomized clinical trial evaluated preoperative administration of the HIF-prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor roxadustat in patients undergoing major elective noncardiac surgery to assess safety, erythropoietic response, and perioperative optimization potential.

- **Accelerated versus daily continuous theta burst stimulation evaluated in crossover trial** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.17.26368336)
  - A transdiagnostic, within-subjects crossover neuroimaging trial (n=34) compared 5 daily sessions against 5 accelerated sessions of continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) targeted to the default mode network, establishing comparable functional connectivity alterations across protocols.

- **Melatonin pilot feasibility trial in cardiac surgery weaning** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43064884/)
  - A pilot randomized feasibility trial evaluated perioperative melatonin to reduce cardiac arrhythmias, sedative reliance, and mechanical ventilation duration during cardiopulmonary bypass weaning following coronary artery bypass grafting.

- **Quality of life outcomes reported from oral peanut immunotherapy trial** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43065152/)
  - Patient-reported outcome evaluations from the OPIA trial detailed quality-of-life dynamics and burden shifts among pediatric participants undergoing protocol-driven oral peanut immunotherapy.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Biotech]** **Erasca advances pan-KRAS program toward Phase 3, targeting Revolution's Rasonque** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/erasca-kras-pancreatic-cancer-drug-results-revolution-rasonque/875314/)
  - Erasca reported new clinical data for its pan-KRAS inhibitor program in pancreatic cancer as the company prepares to enter Phase 3 clinical development.
  - Erasca is positioning its asset directly against Revolution Medicines' RAS inhibitor Rasonque (rasamtiptinib), aiming to address efficacy duration and resistance limitations observed in early RAS inhibitor readouts.

- **Target trial emulation confirms post-hip fracture anti-osteoporosis mortality benefit** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43064845/)
  - A target trial emulation study assessing post-hip fracture anti-osteoporosis therapy demonstrated significant reductions in all-cause mortality and subsequent fracture risk relative to untreated cohorts.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[Biotech]** **FDA issues Complete Response Letter rejecting Capricor Therapeutics' Duchenne cell therapy** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/20/fda-rejects-capricor-duchenne-therapy/?utm_campaign=rss)
  - The FDA rejected Capricor Therapeutics' biologics license application for its cell therapy candidate intended to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD).
  - Capricor issued a formal response maintaining confidence in its clinical trial data integrity and plans to seek regulatory path clarification with the agency.

- **FDA grants first generic approval for difelikefalin injection** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-and-biologic-approval-and-ind-activity-reports/first-generic-drug-approvals)
  - FDA approved Qilu Pharmaceutical's ANDA for difelikefalin injection, marking the first generic equivalent to Korsuva for moderate-to-severe pruritus associated with chronic kidney disease in adult hemodialysis patients.

- **Greenwich Rx issues voluntary nationwide recall of compounded sterile products** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/safety/recalls-market-withdrawals-safety-alerts/greenwich-rx-issues-voluntary-nationwide-recall-compounded-sterile-products-due-lack-sterility)
  - 503A compounding pharmacy Greenwich Rx voluntarily recalled all unexpired lots of compounded sterile products—including formulations produced for Clove Rx—at the consumer level due to potential lack of sterility assurance.

- **Breckenridge Pharmaceutical recalls propranolol ER capsules over potential particulate contamination** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/safety/recalls-market-withdrawals-safety-alerts/breckenridge-pharmaceutical-inc-issues-voluntary-nationwide-consumer-level-recall-one-lot)
  - Breckenridge Pharmaceutical voluntarily recalled one lot of Propranolol Hydrochloride Extended-Release Capsules USP (60 mg, manufactured by Adare Pharma Solutions) due to potential metal contamination.

- **FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine issues Warning Letter to feedlot operator** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/warning-letters/ogle-cattle-company-inc-713311-09052025)
  - FDA CVM issued a Warning Letter to Texas-based Ogle Cattle Company following inspections detailing unapproved animal drug usage and FD&C Act regulatory violations.

## Business & Strategy

- **[Biotech]** **Compass Pathways and Usona Institute navigate commercialization race for first FDA-approved psilocybin** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/race-first-psilocybin-blockbuster-compass-usona/875369/)
  - Compass Pathways and the non-profit Usona Institute are advancing lead psilocybin programs toward potential initial FDA approvals in major depressive disorder and treatment-resistant depression.
  - Commercial viability across the emerging class remains heavily dependent on resolving post-approval delivery logistics, specialized site REMS requirements, competitive drug pricing, and commercial payer coverage policies.

## Public Health & Policy

- **CMS launches Medicare pilot to evaluate lifestyle and nutritional interventions for chronic disease** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/20/kennedy-food-is-medicine-maha-elevate-pilot/?utm_campaign=rss)
  - Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services introduced the "Elevate" pilot program, testing coverage for structured lifestyle, preventative, and "food is medicine" interventions to alter chronic disease trajectories.

- **Public health perspective urges MAHA leadership to champion MMR vaccination** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/21/rfk-jr-maha-measles-outbreak-elimination-status-promote-mmr-vaccine/?utm_campaign=rss)
  - A STAT opinion piece outlined actionable policy steps for HHS leadership and the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement to reinforce national measles elimination status through active promotion of the MMR vaccine.

- **Comparative evaluation identifies structural gaps in US and UK drug safety communications** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43064863/)
  - Comparative pharmacovigilance analysis evaluating FDA and UK MHRA safety communications using dapsone demonstrated significant variations in risk messaging timeline, update frequency, and risk communication frameworks for dermatologic drugs.

- **ICE detention of Princeton researcher sparks concern over international scientific mobility** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/20/princeton-researcher-eva-yi-xie-ice-detention-rattles-interational-scholars/?utm_campaign=rss)
  - The immigration detention of Princeton neuroscience researcher Eva Yi Xie following return travel from an academic conference has raised operational concerns across academic institutions regarding international scholar workforce stability.

***

**Worth watching:** Erasca's pan-KRAS clinical trial data presentation as it positions to challenge Revolution Medicines' Rasonque in Phase 3 pancreatic cancer development.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [Creatine and a Stressed Brain](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/NJSIzIDP0kA) -- Physionic
        - A randomized trial revealed that a single dose of creatine can improve cognitive performance during sleep deprivation, challenging the notion that tissue accumulation over weeks is required for benefits.
        - Creatine supports the brain's energy availability under stress, helping to mitigate sleep-deprivation-induced impairments in memory, attention, and cognitive function.
        - While 5 grams per day is the standard dose for physical performance, cognitive research often uses higher doses (20 grams or more), and single-dose cognitive benefits cannot be assumed to occur at standard 5-gram supplementation levels.
- Pure Science
    - [What Darwin Never Saw Coming: Punctuated Equilibrium](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/hLHHd8F7aXk) -- Quanta Magazine
        - A new mathematical model indicates that evolution often proceeds through rapid bursts of change rather than purely gradual progression, supporting the theory of punctuated equilibrium.
        - The model reveals that evolutionary changes are coupled with branching processes across multiple granularities of systems.
        - Researchers observed evidence of these punctuated dynamics across diverse domains, including biological subjects like enzymes and cephalopods, as well as linguistic systems like Indo-European languages.
    - [21 - Hero  #mathctober](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PZsbmvh_p38) -- El Jj
        - This video serves as the final entry for the channel's "mathctober" content series.
        - The thematic connection to the word "hero" (héros) links the mathematical topic to a broader narrative thread.
        - The subject matter acts as explicit foreshadowing for the topic of the channel's upcoming long-form video.
- Tech & Engineering
    - [Cette limite physique va faire tomber Nvidia](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7Jk8FFFqLW0) -- Underscore_
        - The video discusses physical constraints threatening GPU maker Nvidia and competition from specialized alternative microchips, including hardware from a French startup.
        - The discussion features guest Steeve Morin from ZML alongside references to machine learning optimization platforms and specialized chip architectures like Vsora.
        - It highlights optimized deployment setups for running applications efficiently outside traditional hardware paradigms.
